name: Jacob
overview: Jacob is a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, noted specifically as the son of Matthan within the lineage of the Messiah. His identity is grounded in his role within this messianic genealogy as recorded in Matthew 1:15. No additional personal notes are provided beyond his tribal and genealogical significance.
namesAndTitles: The name Jacob means 'follower, replacer, one who follows at the heel,' reflecting its Hebrew roots. This proper name was not given by God but is significant in identifying his role in biblical history, as referenced in Matthew 1:15.
familyAndRelationships: Jacob is identified as the son of Matthan, an inferred relationship from Matthew 1:15, and as the father of Joseph, explicitly stated in Matthew 1:16. These connections place him directly within the messianic lineage leading to Christ.
scriptureSignificance: Jacob holds a critical place in Scripture as a key link in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, highlighting God's sovereign choice in the unfolding of redemptive history. His placement in the tribe of Judah and as an ancestor of Joseph underscores his role in the covenant lineage. Though not elaborated here, his life exemplifies God's grace working through imperfect individuals to fulfill divine promises.
